name: ABS-AF

summary.text: ABS-AF is aramid-fibre-filled ABS. Makers sell it for lighter, fibre-reinforced parts that are easier to print, and stress its dimensional stability and low warping. Its glass transition is 110 °C. On the H2C it prints at 250⁠–⁠270 °C, and a maker recommends a ruby or hardened nozzle while another calls the fibre less abrasive than carbon or glass.

items.text: 10% Aramid fiber reinforced, high rigidity & impact strength, excellent dimensional stability

The applied modifications led to reduced shrinkage, excellent adhesion to work platforms and reduced material density, which means that the printed elements are slightly lighter than their counterparts made with standard ABS.
ABS KEVLAR has been designed for 3D printing by a precise formulation of aramid fibers into ABS materials.
The aramid fibers assuring dimensional stability ,preventing the printed object to warp and even make the printed object lighter than regular ABS .

items.text: Create aramid fibre reinforced 3D prints that are lighter, more resistant, and easier to print compared to native ABS, thank to Nanovia ABS AF.
Lighter prints compared to native ABS
Higher mechanical resistances compared to native ABS
Increased resistance to friction and shocks
For an outdoor usage, we recommend that you paint your print or submit them to an anti UV treatment, such as our Nanovia smoothing solution.
Aramdid fibers and ABS are sensitive to UV radiation.
Thanks to the aramid fibers Nanovia ABS AF allows for excellent 3D printing properties with limited warping and a great bed adhesion.
Low warping when printing (even less than with carbon fiber composites)
A less abrasive fiber compared to carbon and glass
Whilst printing ABS produces a VOC derivative of styrene.
